Five coding-agent-eligible repos (>=3000 stars): shadcn/improve (5), addyosmani/agent-skills (5), vercel-labs/agent-browser (5), openai/codex-security (4), homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp (3). All five were archived (cap 5 of 5); none was eligible-not-archived. The other 5 entries were rejected (design-system library, stock-analysis app, finance app, Java algorithms collection, and GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src at 1,800 stars, below the 3,000 threshold).

Never re-clone rule applied: check_unmodified passed for all three already-archived repos before the same-volume move. addyosmani/agent-skills was unchanged; agent-browser was upgraded d129226 -> 51b6f8a and ha-mcp 6b14aca -> 59cec3e (with its pinned submodule) by incremental git fetch, previous manifests kept as previous-*.json. Nothing moved to Trash; no user-edited copies found.
git-lfs is still not installed on this Mac; none of today's archived trees contain LFS pointers. Repository code, hooks, installers and dependencies were never run.
Two new featured recommendations: shadcn/improve and openai/codex-security (never featured). The other archived repos were featured earlier or are not featured (ha-mcp, rated 3).

featured.reason: shadcn's improve (MIT): a single Agent Skill (Claude Code plugin manifest included; installs with `npx skills add shadcn/improve`) that maps a repo, fans out parallel audit subagents across nine categories, re-vets every file:line finding, and writes self-contained plans in plans/ with verification-gate commands, out-of-scope lists and STOP conditions so a cheaper model can execute them. Includes /improve branch, next, execute (isolated worktree + review) and reconcile. Directly useful advisor/executor workflow for coding agents.
ideas: Install it with `npx skills add shadcn/improve`, run `/improve quick` on ai-daily-radar with your strongest model, then hand the top plan to a cheaper model with `/improve execute 001`, which works in an isolated git worktree and reviews the diff before you merge.
Run `/improve branch` before merging changes to the v1 WebView Android app so the audit only covers what the branch changed, with file:line evidence for each finding.
Point `/improve next` at the daily routine and publish scripts to get feature ideas backed by evidence from the repo; rejected ideas are recorded with reasons so they don't come back next run.
Study skills/improve/references/plan-template.md (inlined context, verification-gate commands, STOP conditions, commit drift stamp) and use the same format when you hand tasks between your bots.

Add a DESIGN.md describing the site's original pre-glass design: improve's recon reads DESIGN.md/PRODUCT.md, so decided tradeoffs aren't re-flagged and the agent's suggestions stay within your design rules.

featured.reason: OpenAI's Codex Security (Apache-2.0): a Codex plugin with 20 security skills (security-scan, security-diff-scan, deep-security-scan, threat-model, threat-model-visualize, triage, fix-finding, verify-fix, define-security-policy and more) plus the `cs` CLI, TypeScript SDK, GitHub Action, SARIF/JSON/CSV export and scanner-import guides. Rated 4 rather than 5 because scans need an OpenAI/Codex sign-in or API key and paid model usage (Node 22.13+/24/26 and Python 3.10+).
ideas: Enable the Codex Security plugin in Codex (`/plugins`) and run `$security-diff-scan` (or `cs scan . --diff origin/main`) on ai-daily-radar before merging changes to the publish pipeline.

Run `$threat-model` and `$threat-model-visualize` on the Android WebView app to map risks such as JavaScript bridges, URL loading and mixed content, then use `$fix-finding` and `$verify-fix` on what it confirms.
Use `cs policy .` to draft a SECURITY.md for the portfolio and client repos you show employers; it writes the draft outside the repo so you review it before copying it in.

Copy github-action/examples/repository.yml into a MacApex repo as a weekly scan with the CODEX_SECURITY_API_KEY secret and the example's ~$5 per-scan limit, and export SARIF so findings appear in GitHub code scanning.
Read plugins/codex-security/skills/ together with evals/check-skills to learn how a 20-skill plugin is organized and tested, and use that layout for your own shared skills such as CLI-Anything.

news_highlights.why_it_matters: One searchable, synced history for agent sessions across machines, so you can start a task in Claude Code and resume it in Codex. Handy if you work across a Mac mini, a MacBook and the box.

news_highlights.why_it_matters: A major consumer brand is pushing back on browser agents, citing security and federal rules. Expect more sites to block agent traffic, which affects anyone building agent-driven web automation.

news_highlights.title: Gemini Decisions API
